questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Something outside of Europe. The travel opportunities and the weather

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to navigate through the sent emails from the representative of the host university. Just pin them in outlook.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I don't know if I was just lucky, but it was fairly easy. I used Flatmates.

There are also tons of facebook groups with plenty of opportunities. Also, as an exchange student people might try to charge extra in rent, so always try to negotiate price.

Always verify the person you are in contact with, either in person or through a video call. Never pay anything until you are 100% they are not scamming you.

I recommend living in Glebe, Newtown, Surry Hills, Darlinghurst or Paddington. Those areas were very nice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend living off campus, because you can likely find some better deals in terms of rent, space and local area. You get to have a much more local experience and you get to learn about your area in a different way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use them.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to get a USI and fill out some information on the host institution's system. It was fairly straightforward and the representative that will take care of you, will send you all the necessary details.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always email the one taking care of you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted and I even dropped and added a class. Everything was easy and simple. Just make sure to do it in time for the deadline.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was fairly simple, so I have none. Just don't panic, and make sure your USI information aligns with the information you put into USYD's system, otherwise you'll be asked to do it again.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fairly easy, but I still got a lot out of it. It depends on the classes you take.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was less theoretical and more practical examples were used during the lecture.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sport and Learning in Australian culture
Learning in Outdoor education
Japanese 1
Foundations of Data science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sport and Learning in Australian culture
Learning in Outdoor education

These are not that challenging to get through, but you still get a lot out of it. You get to experience the sport culture of Australia which is a very unique experience. You get to learn about the environment and you also get to experience it with field trips. You get to know many of the other exchange students, because these courses are specifically catered towards exchange students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were markets and food trucks at campus sometimes. Sometimes there were other fun events during the day.

There were parties and the societies offered field trips and other events as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The markets were fun and on of the parties was fun because you get to socialise with people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Things to do in Australia: 
Hunter valley wine region: book a nice villa with your friends, it's a fun time.
Blue mountains - specifically the grand canyon track and wentworth falls.
Tasmania - Visit Tasmania and rent a campervan. 
Surf camp
Melbourne - Fitzroy and Brunswick 

Other:
Bali - Ubud and Uluwatu

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No, just do it I guess.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
They walk and drive on the left side. The escalators are on the left side. It took some time of getting used to.

The nightlife is very different than in Copenhagen. You can easily get rejected if you don't seem sober enough and you should always bring ID even if you are just buying alcohol. Everything closes fairly early.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to get your own housing in a share house. Chances are you get something cozy and a lot bigger than the dorms. Just make sure to still be in the center or around campus, so you can easily go and hangout with your friends. You get to experience the city and life in a more local way which I greatly appreciated. 

Don't spend too much time getting caught up with the most challenging courses. Spend more time experiencing the city and socialise with different people.

Schedule your timetable in a way, where you are done early in the week.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Get the concession Opal card, because it is way cheaper.

Uber is cheap.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting the opportunity to study and live in a different country and experience a different culture. Also to meet all kinds of sweet people both local and exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
